chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), why did he not reclaim Fadak when he assumed authority over the people? He said: Because we are the People of the House, and our Guardian is Allah, the Exalted and Mighty; He alone will take our rights from those who oppress us. And we are the guardians of the believers; we only judge for them and take their rights from those who oppress them, and we do not take for ourselves. And I have presented the reasons for this in my book 'Illal al-Shara'i' (The Causes of the Laws), 'Al-Ahkam wa al-Asbab', and I have restricted myself in this book to what was narrated from al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding it.

key_terms.عِلَلُ الشَّرَائِعِ: Causes of the Laws (a scholarly work)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali not take Fadak for himself?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) withheld reclaiming Fadak not due to weakness, but to distinguish between divine guardianship (wilayah) and personal ownership. As the Imams are the trustees of the believers' rights, they prioritize rectifying the community's injustices over securing their own material wealth, a principle rooted in their spiritual detachment (zuhd) and unique status as Allah's direct deputies.
